The first generation EBC consisted of a mullite bond coat and yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) top coat.
The second generation EPM EBCs consisted of a silicon first bond coat, a mullite or mullite+BSAS second bond coat, and a BSAS top coat.
The EPM EBCs have accumulated over 24,000 hours of operation in gas turbine engines without failure, with a maximum combustor liner temperature of 1250°C.
BSAS was identified as a promising EBC candidate due to its close CTE match with silicon-based ceramics and low silica activity.
The BSAS-silica reaction produced a thick reaction zone and large pores at the BSAS/silica interface, leading to EBC delamination.
The mullite+BSAS/BSAS EBC exhibited excellent durability up to 1000 hours at 1300°C, with limited BSAS-silica reaction and no pore formation.
The formation of low-melting glasses due to the BSAS-silica reaction was a key life-limiting factor for the mullite+BSAS/BSAS EBC system at temperatures above 1400°C.
The mullite/BSAS EBC showed a porous structure degradation of the BSAS top coat at temperatures above 1400°C, which became severe at 1500°C.

The silica volatilization rate of the BSAS top coat, as measured by thermogravimetric analysis, increased with temperature, with a projected recession of 4, 18, and 72 μm after 1000 hours at 1300, 1400, and 1500°C, respectively, under high-pressure burner rig conditions.
